lessons.title: Where is Cameroon? Regions and capitals
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level II (Class 4) — Social Studies; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Say where Cameroon is and name some neighbours.
Name the ten regions and their capitals.
Name the capital city and the official languages.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; names and dates to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Regional capitals are standard facts; the number of regions (10) reflects the current administrative structure.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Location
blocks.md: Cameroon is in **Central Africa**, near the **Equator**. It has a coast on the **Atlantic Ocean**. Its neighbours are **Nigeria** (west), **Chad** (north-east), the **Central African Republic** (east) and the **Republic of the Congo**, **Gabon** and **Equatorial Guinea** (south). The capital is **Yaoundé**. The official languages are **English and French**.

blocks.caption: The ten regions of Cameroon and their capitals.
blocks.alt: Ten boxes. Each shows a region and its capital: Adamawa, Ngaoundéré; Centre, Yaoundé; East, Bertoua; Far North, Maroua; Littoral, Douala; North, Garoua; North-West, Bamenda; West, Bafoussam; South, Ebolowa; South-West, Buea.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.md: There are **10 regions**. Two are English-speaking: the **North-West** (capital Bamenda) and the **South-West** (capital Buea). **Douala** is the biggest city and main port. Each region has a regional capital and is divided into smaller units (divisions).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that Douala is the capital of Cameroon: it is Yaoundé.
- Mixing a region with its capital.
- Writing *Northwest* in different ways: use *North-West*.
- Forgetting that Cameroon has ten regions.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What is the capital of the West Region?
steps: Look at the list of regions and capitals.
The West Region has Bafoussam as its capital.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name two neighbours of Cameroon and say in which direction each lies.

objectives: Name the four main directions and the points in between.
Read a simple map using its key and a grid.
Draw a simple plan of the classroom.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; names and dates to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
The grid map is an invented example (not a real place).
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Directions
blocks.md: The four main directions (**cardinal points**) are **north (N), east (E), south (S) and west (W)**. In between are north-east (NE), south-east (SE), south-west (SW) and north-west (NW). The Sun **rises in the east** and **sets in the west**. A **compass** has a needle that points north.

blocks.caption: The compass rose.
blocks.alt: A compass rose with arrows north and south, east and west, and the points NE, NW, SE and SW marked between them.

blocks.title: Reading a map
blocks.md: A **map** is a drawing of a place seen from above. Read the **title** and the **key** (what each symbol means). **Grid references** use a letter for the column and a number for the row, written like **B3**. Always start with the **letter**. Maps use **symbols** (a square for a school, a blue line for a river) and a **scale**.

blocks.caption: A simple map with a grid.
blocks.alt: A four by four grid with letters A to D across the top and numbers 1 to 4 down the side. The school is in B2, the market in C1, the river in D3 and the health centre in C3.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that the Sun rises in the west.
- Writing a grid reference with the number first: write **B3**, not 3B.
- Not using the key.
- Thinking that a map shows what you see from the side.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: If you face north, in which direction is your right hand?
steps: Imagine the compass: north is in front, east is to the right.
Your right hand points to the east.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: On the grid map, what is in square C1?

lessons.title: Land, rivers and climate of Cameroon
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level II (Class 4) — Social Studies; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe the main kinds of land in Cameroon.
Name Mount Cameroon and some rivers.
Describe the hot wet south and the hotter drier north.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; names and dates to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Examples are simplified; see the Class 5 Social Studies and FSLC pack for more detail.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Relief
blocks.md: Cameroon has a low **coastal plain** by the Atlantic, **plateaus** in the centre and south, **highlands** with hills and mountains in the West and North-West, and flatter, drier land in the **north**. **Mount Cameroon** (also called Fako) is the highest mountain; it is an **active volcano** in the South-West Region.

blocks.caption: Kinds of land in Cameroon.
blocks.alt: A table with relief or zone, where, and an example: coast near Limbe and Kribi, highlands in the West and North-West, volcano Mount Cameroon in the South-West, savanna in Adamawa and the North, rainforest in the South and East.

blocks.title: Rivers and climate
blocks.md: Important rivers are the **Sanaga**, the **Wouri**, the **Benue** and the **Logone**; **Lake Chad** is in the far north. The **south** is **hot and wet**, with **two rainy seasons**. The **north** is **hotter and drier**, with **one rainy season**. The highlands are cooler. In the dry season the dusty **Harmattan** wind blows from the north.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that Cameroon has the same weather everywhere.
- Thinking that all of Cameroon is rainforest.
- Putting Mount Cameroon in the north.
- Saying that the Wouri flows to Lake Chad (it flows into the Atlantic).

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: In which region is Mount Cameroon?
steps: Mount Cameroon is near Buea and Limbe.
Buea and Limbe are in the South-West Region.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Why can cocoa grow in the south but cotton grows better in the north?
steps: Cocoa needs a lot of rain and warmth: the south is wet.
Cotton needs a long sunny dry season: the north is drier.
blocks.answer: Cocoa likes the wet south; cotton likes the drier north.
